$comment: Flow guards, dogfooded on Beadloom itself (BDL-061 S1, rebound in .35).
These entries are written by `beadloom setup-agentic-flow` and are the EXACT
artifact an adopter gets: the command runs the emitted .claude/hooks/beadloom-guard.sh,
not `beadloom guard` directly. Until .35 this file registered the direct command, so the
adapter we ship had never run here and 'dogfooded' was evidence about a path adopters
do not use, which is why #170's narrower matcher went unnoticed for five review cycles.
The hook carries NO logic: it pipes the harness event to `beadloom guard`, which reads
the declarations, strictness and exclusions from .beadloom/flow.yml. Adding or retiring a
guard is a flow.yml edit plus a re-run of setup-agentic-flow, never a hand edit here.
Exit codes map to the harness by design: 0 pass/skip, 1 warn (surfaced, not blocking),
2 block. Both guards ship at `warn`, so nothing here stops work today; they report, and
they name what they did not check. The matcher is the shipped one, and since BDL-068 S4
(#170) it names Bash as well: a file written through `python3 - <<EOF`, `sed -i` or a
redirection is an edit, and until that bead it fired no guard at all while --liveness
reported every guard healthy. `beadloom guard --liveness` now reads this matcher back
off disk and reports which of the write paths the emitted role adapters grant it can
see, so a narrower matcher here is a reported gap rather than a silence.
